correctness.rationale: Under the stipulated biased nearest-neighbor mutation and finite equal-mortality set, irreducibility of the stationary equation makes a nonzero nonnegative solution positive. Summing it gives tm=m−(1−d)sum_S x, hence 0<t=λ(1−m)<1. The ℓ¹ Neumann inverse on this range reduces the equation to the finite Green principal matrix, and positivity and strict increase of its Perron root give precisely one root below 1 iff d<d_*(S). At the endpoint the Green entries are δ⁻¹ times 1 for i≥j or (q/p)^(j−i) otherwise; conjugation by diag(s^(−a_i)) gives the similarity with symmetric K_S/δ. The resolvent reconstructs the unique normalized profile, and its required mass 1−t/λ is positive precisely for λ>t. Strict Perron comparison proves unique optimal clustering; principal submatrix monotonicity is strict (extending the positive eigenvector by zero cannot be a top eigenvector of the larger positive matrix). Finite row sums are strictly below the infinite geometric sum. Independently, the cosine profile cos((i−(k+1)/2)θ) is positive for θ∈(0,π/k) and the ghost condition yields tan(kθ/2)tan(θ/2)=(1−s)/(1+s), equivalent to the displayed quantization. With θ=π/k+O(k⁻²), the mortality deficit is exactly 2sδ(1−cos θ)/(1−s²), giving π²√(pq)/k² to leading order. As d approaches threshold from below, t→1 and the normalized favorable-site mass tends to zero. The endpoint Green formula is summable uniformly in t≤1 on every left half-line j≤J for each source in S, proving directed escape, not equilibrium at equality. In the two-site example the threshold condition reduces to 3^(−L/2)>1/4; for L=1 the symmetric off-diagonal Green factor is 1/2 at the root, giving t=8/(5√3) and the recorded mass. value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact feasibility boundary for a natural deterministic model, distinguishes finite favorable geometries at fixed size, quantifies the finite-size gap to the infinite-block ceiling, and explains why positive total population in the parameter limit does not produce a stationary ℓ¹ limit. The global classification and escape law are useful beyond the illustrative example, without purporting to predict transient stability or stochastic survival.
